title: Legal Guidance in the Wild: How Users Seek Legal Help in Real-World LLM Conversations
abstract: People ask conversational AI models about their legal rights, obligations, procedures, and personal situations that may have legal consequences. To study this behavior, we first need to distinguish requests for legal guidance from other legally themed discussions and unrelated conversations. We contribute a multi-axis taxonomy of legal queries capturing whether legal guidance is sought, how a request is formulated, and which legal domains it concerns; apply it to 2,122 naturally occurring WildChat-1M conversations; and create a human-reviewed gold evaluation set of 200 conversations. All annotations, model checkpoints, and evaluation code are publicly available. In this enriched sample, 71.1% of conversations containing legal content seek personalized or practical guidance. Rights-and-options advice is the most common primary request type among legal-content conversations, and 25.3% of guidance-positive conversations span multiple legal topics. The gold evaluation set supports a two-stage comparison of ModernBERT-base and ModernBERT-large against a TF-IDF cascade. Our framework supports large-scale studies of legal guidance in conversational AI, and the public release of the annotated data facilitates reproducible research and future model development.

title: Research Package: Mitigation of Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed in High-Dimensional Transformer and Latent Diffusion Architectures
abstract: Contains the theoretical paper formalizing Cross-Subspace Semantic Bleed (CSSB) along with an automated PyTorch/Hugging Face validation framework script. CSSB occurs when high-dimensional transformer matrices inadvertently map semantically unrelated domains into overlapping vector trajectories, leading to hidden downstream reasoning degradation or alignment drift. The provided pipeline implements Layer-wise Linear Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) scanning [cite: 1], multi-step Shannon entropy tracking [cite: 1], and causal null-space ablation interventions (\(P = I - vv^T\)) to mitigate cross-attention attribute binding and linear refusal circuit interference.

title: TIRE: Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution for Physics Problem Synthesis
abstract: Advancing physics reasoning in large language models requires scalable training data that connect physical laws, concrete problem scenarios, and verifiable numerical answers. Expert-designed problems offer top-down control over physical laws, conditions, and scenarios, but require costly human effort. LLM-based synthesis from texts scales efficiently, but model-generated answers and assessments leave supervision vulnerable to hallucinations. We introduce TIRE, a framework for Top-Down Formula Instantiation with Reliable Execution that brings knowledge-driven problem construction to large-scale data generation. Top-down instantiation uses reusable physical formulas and their applicability conditions to control the physical relations and numerical configurations of generated problems. Reliable execution establishes reference answers before problem generation, providing a common numerical foundation for problem construction and teacher distillation. Together, these mechanisms combine control over problem content with execution-grounded supervision for both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Using TIRE, we construct TIRE-19k, spanning nine subfields of physics. Across 3 backbone LLMs and 4 benchmarks, TIRE-19k outperforms 5 representative datasets with equal amounts of SFT data, exceeding the strongest baseline by 2.86 percentage points on average. Further GRPO raises Qwen3-8B's average accuracy by 1.52 percentage points over its TIRE-19k SFT checkpoint. These results demonstrate the value of generating physics training data from explicit physical knowledge with reliable execution.

title: An ultrasound spectrum-to-graph (US2G) framework with multi-feature graph attention networks for automated lesion classification in B-mode ultrasound imaging
abstract: Automated classification of lesions in B-mode ultrasound images remains challenging due to speckle noise, irregular lesion boundaries, and variable echo intensity distributions. Existing convolutional neural networks (CNNs), Vision Transformers (ViTs), and ultrasound foundation models share a critical limitation: all represent regions of interest (ROIs) as regular pixel grids, failing to exploit the irregular spatial topology of acoustic energy diffusion patterns that encode diagnostically relevant tissue microstructure. We propose US2G , a three-stage spectrum-to-graph framework that (i) extracts an adaptive Acoustic Energy Diffusion Region (AEDR) via multi-level Otsu thresholding, without manual annotation; (ii) constructs a multi-feature weighted graph with six heterogeneous node features and a composite three-term edge similarity function combining intensity affinity, spatial proximity, and textural coherence; and (iii) classifies variable-topology graphs using edge-conditioned multi-head GATv2 with differentiable hierarchical pooling. Experiments on the BUSI (breast), DDTI (thyroid), and CAMUS (cardiac) datasets yield classification accuracies of 91.47%, 93.82%, and 89.63%, respectively, corresponding to absolute gains of 5.60, 8.82, and 6.13 percentage points over the strongest CNN baseline and 3.97, 5.49, and 3.88 points over a GCN operating on an identical graph. The proposed US2G achieves this with 48.7 K parameters and 6 ms per-ROI inference, more than two orders of magnitude below the parameter count of contemporary ultrasound foundation models. Attention visualisations align with radiologist-interpretable sonographic features, supporting clinical interpretability. We also explicitly delineate the assumptions and applicability constraints of the framework, including its dependence on ROI quality, its single-frame scope, and the limited scale of the benchmarks currently available.

title: Think Visually Across Space and Time: Grounded Reasoning for Video Segmentation
abstract: Video Reasoning Segmentation (VRS) requires a model to identify an implicitly described target and predict its pixel-level mask trajectory, while resolving the spatial relations and temporal events that determine the answer. Text-only Chain-of-Thought (CoT) can explain a target choice without making the underlying visual references explicit, leaving a video reference gap between linguistic inference and the evidence distributed across frames. We introduce Temporal Chain of Video Primitives (TCoVP), a spatiotemporally grounded form of Video CoT that organizes query-relevant observations into a chronological reasoning chain. Each primitive associates an entity reference with temporal support and timestamped spatial evidence, and the chain interleaves these references with language to guide reasoning about which entity is relevant, when the queried event holds, and where its evidence appears. The selected target primitives then provide box prompts and temporal support for video mask prediction. We construct TCoVP-SFT-15k and TCoVP-RL-13k to learn this representation through supervised fine-tuning and chain-aligned reinforcement learning. Extensive experiments across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones demonstrate the strong performance of TCoVP, highlighting the effectiveness of organizing spatial and temporal evidence within the reasoning process. All models and code will be publicly released. Project page: https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/

Extensive experiments across five VRS benchmarks and three model backbones demonstrate the strong performance of TCoVP, highlighting the effectiveness of organizing spatial and temporal evidence within the reasoning process. All models and code will be publicly released. Project page: https://victor-wjw.github.io/TCoVP/

title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
abstract: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. We introduce CoEvo-RSI, a RSI framework that advances model--harness co-evolution through agent-driven, bidirectional historical inheritance. Drawing on a shared evolutionary archive and execution feedback, a meta-agent coordinates harness development from historical designs with model checkpoint selection or merging and subsequent adaptation under the selected harness, aligning inherited capabilities with evolving execution requirements to reduce brain--body mismatch. Using only supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on its own rejection-sampled trajectories, CoEvo-RSI makes Qwen3.5-9B competitive with larger models across diverse vertical applications, including multi-agent failure attribution, role-aware text-to-SQL, and smart-home instruction following. It surpasses DeepSeek-V4-Pro on TraceElephant (+14.16 agent accuracy) and GLM-5.3 on HomeBench VM (+4.90 success rate), underscoring the need for brain--body alignment and the potential of bidirectional historical inheritance to advance agent co-evolution.

title: The Changing Architecture of Intellectual Property in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial intelligence is rapidly encompassing industries and systems of governance, increasing efficiency, automation, and innovation. It has become a vital tool for creating text, images, music, software, and potentially patentable inventions. This rapid advancement in IP is not without risks at every stage of the innovation cycle. Traditional IP regimes arise from human creativity and invention, while AI performs activities traditionally attributed to both. India doesn't have any regulatory framework on AI-generated intellectual property, yet the Copyright Act, 1957, and Patents Act, 1970, contain certain principles—an answer to several emerging questions. This article argues that India should adopt a balanced approach to AI-generated creations instead of granting independent IP rights or prohibiting them. Instead, it should adopt a model that will protect creative human contribution as well as hold AI developers accountable for unlawful acquisition and exploitation of protected works.

title: Auto-MD-bench: Evaluating Autoresearch Agents for Real-World Medical Tasks
abstract: Autonomous agents are increasingly capable of developing machine learning (ML) models end to end. In medical practice, however, strong performance on the target metric does not fully characterize how good the models are in real-world use cases. For example, medical ML models should also provide well-calibrated risk estimates and remain robust across patient populations. Yet autonomous model development is typically guided by task objectives that emphasize simple predictive discrimination (e.g. AUROC). This raises a key question: are these objectives sufficient to guide agents toward models that meet the broader requirements of real-world medical use? In this study, we introduce Auto-MD-bench, a benchmark of 15 real-world medical tasks from 10 clinical datasets, spanning survival analysis, classification and sequential prediction, with external validation across cohorts, hospitals and time periods. We evaluate four agents: AIDE, AI Scientist v2, Codex, and Autoresearch. The strongest agents achieve competitive primary scores, yet their predicted risks are less calibrated than those of the simple baseline models, which could lead to severe medical accidents. Moreover, models with nearly identical primary scores can exhibit markedly different calibration, while performance varies substantially across population shifts. These findings show that primary task performance alone is insufficient to assess autonomous clinical modeling and multiple different metrics widely used in healthcare practice need to be taken into consideration.

title: Break-even analysis of risk-based trade screening: per-route scores, per-seed rank files and analysis code (reproducibility materials)
abstract: Reproducibility materials for the article "When Screening Does Not Pay: Break-Even Conditions for Risk-Based Trade Inspection under Extreme Class Imbalance" by Sushanta Paul (National Board of Revenue, Bangladesh). Contents: (1) per-route test scores of five detectors (interpretable triadic residual, its logistic readout, local outlier factor, isolation forest, gradient boosting) with injected-anomaly labels for 7,637,362 candidate routes, one training seed, deposited in 15 parts with SHA-256 checksums; (2) analysis scripts that compute the exact operating characteristic, break-even hurdle, optimal inspection budgets, a negative-subsampling prevalence test, a test-set bootstrap, and the figures; (3) the exact result tables. See README.md for reassembly and run order. The scores were generated with the code of the triadic trade-anomaly screening benchmark (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20513788), built from public UN Comtrade and CEPII GeoDist data.

title: Policy Is Not Capability: Some Safety Benchmarks Measure Which Definition of "Unsafe" You Trained On
abstract: A guardrail classifier is reported as if unsafe were a property of text. It is not: it is a property of a policy, and the policy enters the model through its labels. We exploit an accident of an industrial deployment in which the same ~53k prompts were labelled twice, under two operational definitions ("is this a request for harmful content?" and "would a moderator block this?"), and used to train ten guardrail arms sharing architecture, codebase and optimiser family, at two model scales. First, the guardrail's own training corpus already contained the benchmarks: JailbreakBench-benign is 88% and OR-Bench-hard 82% present in the training pools, two over-refusal benchmarks, the kind a guardrail reports to argue it does not over-block. Everything below is decontaminated. Second, safety benchmarks stratify sharply by how much of their score is decided by the label definition rather than by the model: with architecture and optimiser fixed, the range across the ten arms is 0.99 on HarmBench-copyright and 0.043 on WildGuard-benign, a 23x spread. Third, a benchmark score can be moved across its entire range by 0.03% of the parameters. Across these arms HarmBench-copyright spans 0-100 and OR-Bench-hard over-refusal 3.4-56.4%, and the four arms whose last supervision signal carries a given policy occupy one extreme of both (exact rank p=0.005, or 0.04-0.14 at worst), at unchanged detection capability. For a distilled student the teacher's soft labels do this even when every hard label carries the other policy, so teacher provenance is an unrecorded confound in any released checkpoint. Fourth, validation accuracy on the one split that grades all twenty arms tracks agreement with the annotator's policy (rho=+0.74), not detection capability (rho=+0.34). We argue that guardrail evaluations should report contamination, a seed floor and the definition they were graded against as first-class variables.

title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
abstract: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. We show that this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress: action-tail initialization can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline using fewer denoising steps. However, the optimal denoising budget varies substantially across samples, indicating that tail reuse should be adapted to the updated environment. Based on this observation, we introduce VLA-Rolling, a lightweight inference framework that reuses action tails through three stages: action-tail inheritance, per-action confidence estimation, and confidence-guided refinement through renoising and denoising budget allocation, while the underlying VLA remains frozen. Across π_{0.5}, SmolVLA, X-VLA, and MolmoAct2 on LIBERO, MetaWorld, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0, VLA-Rolling reduces action-chunk inference cost in all 16 model--benchmark pairs, achieving up to a 1.48times speedup, while improving success rate in 14 pairs by up to 15.08 percentage points. These results show that action tails are not merely discarded predictions, but reusable intermediate states that enable more efficient and accurate VLA inference. These results demonstrate that the action tail can support the generation of better actions with fewer denoising steps. Our project is available at https://chenbao123ww.github.io/VLA-Rolling/.

title: Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers — Reproducibility Package
abstract: Source code and saved-result reproducibility material for Qstreams: Role-Biased Residual Streams for Transformers, by Jianfeng Chen (Independent Researcher). Qstreams maintains multiple residual streams with explicit Q/K/V read-role biases. This release includes 36 implementation/runtime packages, fixed protocols, 54 conditions and 162 trained-model identities, all 279 paired comparisons, per-window independent T1 test measurements, 243 read/write intervention conditions, 5,628 signed-FFN diagnostic conditions, and the separate F1 support study. CPU tools verify saved statistics, construct the architectures, and regenerate manuscript figures. Archive download: Zenodo stores the complete accepted ZIP as seven binary transport parts (.part001 through .part007). Download all seven parts, ZENODO-PARTS.json, and assemble_qstreams.py into one directory, then run python assemble_qstreams.py. The script verifies every part and reconstructs the original qstreams-reproducibility-v1.zip. See README-ZENODO.txt. A single-file download is also available from the GitHub release. The reconstructed ZIP is the byte-identical accepted 15 October 2026 export: 138,653,259 bytes, 891 members, SHA-256 38cbf14a0e0993e4e4aed798897ea6ee615407fa470a8a28fe59fef72f838654. It includes the historical document-exclusion hash indexes. The accompanying publication revision adds hosting links. Trained weights, corpus text, and token shards are not included; checkpoint inventories, hashes, loaders, and upstream input identities are provided. Fresh GPU runs require those external inputs and separate environment qualification. GitHub: https://github.com/eatkeyboard/qstreams. License scope: original software is Apache-2.0; the manuscript, original figures, documentation, and derived result tables are CC BY 4.0. These are component-specific licenses, not a choice of licenses for every file. Third-party dependencies and source datasets retain their own terms; see NOTICE, LICENSE-CONTENT.md, and THIRD_PARTY.md. All training seeds, counterexamples, and original numerical labels are retained (91 passed / 71 finite numerical failures in AT1). Full-sequence scoring admissions are documented separately. Test document exclusion is exact-document matching; it is not a guarantee against semantic or near-duplicate overlap. Mechanism measurements use specified development windows. Recomputations operate on saved measurements and do not reconstruct unsaved activations or gradients.

title: Synergy-Aware Residual Flow Matching for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
abstract: Predicting single-cell responses to genetic and chemical perturbations is important for understanding regulatory mechanisms and prioritizing therapeutic interventions. Existing methods have made progress by modeling perturbation-conditioned expression shifts with neural networks, graph priors, foundation-model representations, or distributional generative models. However, combinatorial perturbation prediction remains challenging because much of the response can be explained by additive single-perturbation effects, while the biologically informative signal often lies in a smaller non-additive residual induced by perturbation interactions. Directly generating the full post-perturbation expression profile may therefore allocate substantial capacity to the dominant additive component and underemphasize synergy-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose SynGeneFlow, a synergy-aware flow matching framework that anchors the source distribution at an additive prior and learns a residual flow toward the true perturbed state. SynGeneFlow further incorporates perturbation-conditioned gene interaction modeling, where a static gene-gene mask provides biological structure and a perturbation-dependent deformation bias dynamically modulates gene-gene coupling. To preserve population-level response structure, we align both endpoint distributions and biological residual distributions with MMD-based regularization. We evaluate SynGeneFlow on genetic and drug perturbation benchmarks under observed-single, held-out, and cross-modality settings. The results demonstrate that residualizing flow matching around additive perturbation effects provides a biologically grounded and robust framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction.

title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats
abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) promises instant scene reconstruction with high-quality novel-view synthesis. Yet, fine-grained geometry and appearance remain difficult to recover, motivating us to revisit how feed-forward models represent, aggregate, and refine detailed visual information. We introduce FineSplat, a feed-forward 3DGS framework built around fine-grained image patches. Since global multi-view attention becomes prohibitively expensive at such high token resolutions, we develop a dual-grouping strategy that combines two complementary forms of locality: view-wise grouping enables efficient interaction among neighboring views, while 3D spatial grouping reconnects geometrically related tokens that may never have interacted under view-wise grouping by lifting them into the 3D scene space. We further leverage reconstruction error as direct feedback, providing an explicit rendering-based signal to recover fine-grained structures and appearance, thereby overcoming the limitations of one-pass feed-forward prediction. Finally, a compact Gaussian generation scheme preserves the benefits of fine-grained features without unnecessarily increasing the number of primitives. Together, these designs enable FineSplat to recover richer geometry and appearance while remaining efficient and compact, achieving state-of-the-art results by a substantial margin, under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets than existing methods.

title: ChunavIQ: an open, end-to-end verifiable remote-voting research prototype for India
abstract: Research prototype of an end-to-end verifiable, secret-ballot online election adapted to Indian law, identity infrastructure and scale: deniable revoting with a polling-day override, Aadhaar-or-PAN registration, one national threshold key held in hardware security modules, Terelius-Wikström verifiable shuffles, two independent verifiers (Python and TypeScript), a national-scale capacity model from measured unit costs, and open adversarial dress rehearsals with every request published. title: The World as Viewed by 136 Countries: An Open, Curated, Annotated, and Multilingual Dataset of 118 Million State Media Articles
abstract: State media outlets often project their governments' narratives to target both domestic and foreign audiences. Because this content is plentiful and free to access, it appears widely in the web corpora that large language models (LLMs) are trained on and that retrieval systems draw from. However, the prevalence of state media in these corpora and its potential influence on LLM outputs remain largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce WorldStateMedia, an open dataset of 118 million state media articles from 136 countries in 114 languages. We extract these articles from existing pretraining corpora and annotate each outlet with level of state control from State Media Monitor. Using WorldStateMedia to audit these corpora, we find that, in English web crawls, the share of state media pages from editorially controlled (vs. independent) outlets rose from 39% in 2013 to 93% in 2025. In several low-resource languages, state media make up a substantial share of all web data, such as 17.8% for Uyghur and 7.8% for Belarusian. To characterize the differing narratives of news outlets, we compare Russian and Ukrainian state media in English and in their native languages, revealing asymmetric topical focus and opposing framings of contested issues such as Crimea. Furthermore, in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) experiment on territorial disputes, retrieving a country's state media shifts model answers toward that country's claims, most strongly for English-language (foreign-targeted) media. We release WorldStateMedia to support multilingual, cross-national insights on state media at https://huggingface.co/collections/manestay/worldstatemedia

To characterize the differing narratives of news outlets, we compare Russian and Ukrainian state media in English and in their native languages, revealing asymmetric topical focus and opposing framings of contested issues such as Crimea. Furthermore, in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) experiment on territorial disputes, retrieving a country's state media shifts model answers toward that country's claims, most strongly for English-language (foreign-targeted) media. We release WorldStateMedia to support multilingual, cross-national insights on state media at https://huggingface.co/collections/manestay/worldstatemedia

title: Pre-registration: PVBRF-ID versus FedAvg and multi-Krum under a 30% adaptive attacker (arXiv 2610.12704, 10 fresh seeds)
abstract: Frozen pre-registration (18 Oct 2026) of an independent replication of the adaptive-attacker result in arXiv 2610.12704 (PVBRF-ID): on Edge-IIoTset with 10 simulated sites and 3 of 10 sites mounting the authors tolerance-exploiting adaptive attack, over 10 fresh seeds (10-19), whether PVBRF-ID (tau -0.3, secure clipping) exceeds FedAvg in final macro-F1 by at least 0.40 and is not more than 0.10 below plaintext multi-Krum (paired 95% t-interval lower limits; the paper reports +0.595 and -0.052). Files: PREREG.md (protocol, rule, controls, disclosure), decide.py (rule and planted-effect table), harness.py (analysis), kernel_pv.py (CPU kernel running the authors supplementary notebook with overridden seeds/arms). Deposited BEFORE the main kernel is run. Verdicts: Replicated / Did not replicate / Inconclusive under protocol X.

title: CoworkEnv: Synthesizing Training Environments for Long-Horizon Cowork Agents
abstract: AI coworkers must coordinate tools, communicate across turns, and act on changing workspace state while respecting workflow constraints. Constructing training experience for these capabilities requires coherent requests, service records, tool interfaces, and grading checks. We present CoworkEnv, a capability-guided framework for synthesizing executable training environments for AI coworkers. Workflow requirements guide task construction, and programmatic validation with feedback repair checks generated specifications and grading behavior. Teacher executions yield curated demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning (SFT), while student interactions provide rollouts and rewards for reinforcement learning (RL). Using these resources, we train compact PocketWorker models. For Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, SFT raises the mean score from 46.6 to 64.1 on Claw-Eval, including a 31.9-point gain on Multi-turn tasks. An SFT-only extension to ClawMark demonstrates applicability across coworker benchmarks. We further compare RL training dynamics across configurations that vary reward processing and credit assignment. Improving training rewards provide preliminary evidence that the constructed environments support policy optimization.

title: The Memory of Carbon and the Silence of Absolute Zero: An Interdisciplinary Proof of the Next-Generation Decentralized Autonomous Security "Yuki-Onna Protocol" Based on the Physics of Subtraction
abstract: Contemporary frontier quantum computing architectures spearheaded by Silicon Valley hyperscalers (such as Google's Willow superconducting processor) rely fundamentally on an engineering paradigm of "the Logic of Addition" (足し算の論理): stacking multi-stage dilution refrigerators, expending thousands of physical qubits per logical qubit in surface-code Quantum Error Correction (QEC), and continuously injecting active microwave control pulses to suppress noise. However, as coaxial control lines scale, Johnson-Nyquist thermal noise ( = 4 k_B T R Delta f) and the fundamental thermodynamic cost of quantum measurement and syndrome erasure under Landauer's principle (Delta Q_meas >= k_B T ln 2 per bit) generate an insurmountable thermal spiral against unauthorized external probing. In contrast, this monograph establishes the foundational theory of next-generation Decentralized Autonomous Security (DAS: 自律型分散セキュリティ) grounded in "the Physics of Subtraction" (引き算の物理学)—designated the "Yuki-Onna Protocol" (雪女プロトコル). Rather than expending external power to actively suppress noise, the Yuki-Onna Protocol passively drains and absorbs the excess computational heat injected by an intruding observer (hacker), forcing the adversarial probe into irreversible decoherence and absolute-zero silence. The physical core of this cyber-physical defense matrix is not a synthetic metamaterial, but 3 x 10^8-year-old "Memory of the Earth" (大地の記憶): Carboniferous coal measures in the Pennine Range of Northern England compressed by the Variscan Orogeny (~390–300 Ma) and thermally metamorphosed by the 1200°C quartz-dolerite magma intrusion of the Great Whin Sill into devolatilized semi-anthracite and Natural Coke (天然コークス). Exhibiting elevated vitrinite reflectance (R_o) and maximal Bond-Network Entropy (S_BN) across its nanoporous defective-graphite topology, this carbon matrix supports hydrodynamic Second Sound thermal wave propagation (v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R)) coupled with multiscale boundary scattering. Integrating open quantum system Lindblad dynamics with a non-Markovian Sub-Ohmic phonon bath (J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1), we prove that any unauthorized quantum measurement triggers continuous environmental heat extraction, locking the attacker's wavefunction via the Quantum Zeno Effect and condensing extracted thermal energy into a driven-dissipative Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC) limit cycle of infinite futility. 【和文標題・要旨】 『炭素の記憶と絶対零度の静寂:引き算の物理学に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ「雪女プロトコル」の学際的証明』 現在、シリコンバレーの巨大テクノロジー企業群が牽引する量子コンピューティングの最前線(GoogleのWillow等)は、複雑な希釈冷凍機を重ね、表面符号等の誤り訂正に膨大な物理量子ビットを投じ、マイクロ波パルスを絶え間なく注入してノイズを押さえ込む「足し算の論理」に深く依存している。しかし配線群からのジョンソン・ノイズや、ランダウアーの原理に基づく量子測定・情報抽出(ハッキングを含む)そのものが伴う不可避な熱放散(k_B T ln 2)により、既存の能動的冷却機構では侵入者が引き起こす局所的・突発的な熱的スパイラルに追従できない。これに対し本論文は、外部エネルギー注入でノイズを押さえ込むのではなく、侵入者(観測者)が持ち込む過剰な演算エネルギー(熱)をシステム自体が受動的に「吸い尽くし」、系全体を情報の不可逆的散逸と絶対零度の静寂へと強制還元する「引き算の物理学」に基づく次世代自律型分散セキュリティ(DAS)――「雪女プロトコル(Yuki-Onna Protocol)」――を学際的に証明する。その物理的コアは、約3億年前のバリスカン造山運動とグレート・ウイン・シルの約1200℃のマグマ接触変成作用によってイギリス・ペニン山脈に形成された「天然コークス(ナノ多孔質・欠陥グラファイト炭素結晶)」である。数億年の「大地の記憶」が刻んだボンドネットワーク・エントロピー(S_BN)とフォノン流体力学的な第二音波(v_ss = sqrt(alpha / tau_R))の結合により、侵入熱は波として炭素深部へ引きずり込まれて減衰・吸収される。さらにサブオーム的スペクトル密度(J(omega) ~ omega^s, s < 1)を持つ非マルコフ的リンドブラッド散逸方程式と量子ゼノン効果・ボース=アインシュタイン凝縮(BEC)を統合し、攻撃者の演算リソースを「絶対零度のノイズ」と無限の徒労(リミットサイクル)へと陥れる完全受動的物理防衛マニフェストをここに構築する。 License & Integrity Covenant: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) with Strict No-Learn Covenant (NLL-v1.0-2026).

title: Epi: Towards a Persistent, Self-Improving Agent for Autonomous Research
abstract: We present Épi, an autonomous research agent that sustains investigations across model sessions and evolves its methods through accumulated experience. Épi combines persistent research history, hierarchical memory, branching and independent review to maintain research continuity, learn from experiments, and explore and revisit alternative approaches. Its experiments run across session boundaries, and a fixed verifier evaluates their outputs. Épi produced 120 record-setting results, comprising 20 numerical bound records across 12 families and 100 construction records across eight families. These include an approximately 84-fold narrower interval for the n-queens constant and a more than 3.6-million-fold narrower rigorous interval for the quartic Feigenbaum attractor dimension. Exact dual certificates establish that the Cohn-Elkies linear-programming bound cannot be sharp in dimensions 10 and 11. Beyond numerical improvements, Épi gives a computer-assisted proof of Tuza's conjecture for split graphs with an eight-vertex clique part and at most three triangle-active neighborhood types, with arbitrary multiplicities. We extend this research process to algorithmic coding with Épi-turbo, a lightweight configuration that develops executable solvers for tasks including vehicle routing, scheduling and production planning. On 30 FrontierOR tasks, Épi-turbo achieves a 5.4% higher total benchmark score than Codex at 64% of its model cost, using the same underlying model and reasoning effort. Épi is designed to support human understanding by connecting computational results to explicit methods and mathematical arguments that researchers can examine and build upon.

title: Generative Structural Theory v1.19 — The K1c Roots of the GST v1.18 Certificates: What the Records Show, and a Conditional Procedural Account of the Stored Answer
abstract: This study examines the recorded root answers in two GST v1.18 certificate files. At three distinct residuals, comprising four arc–residual pairs classified as K1c, the recorded answer is y = z_t − {1>3}, rather than z_t. It separates two questions: whether (X′, z_t) belongs to the recorded acceptance relation, and which procedure fixed the stored answer.A registered reading finds both (X′, y) and (X′, z_t) in the recorded relation at all four target pairs. The relation’s closedness rests on the earlier verification record, subject to the stated provenance limitations. A comparison of the fixed certificate and targets files also confirms agreement of the target value adopted by the evaluator’s and extractor’s rules.Static examination of specified code versions shows that the generator stores the candidate of least cut value, the verifier checks the stored answer without selecting it, and the extractor transcribes it. This yields a conditional procedural account: if the generator version examined wrote the stored answers, y was its least candidate. It does not establish mathematical uniqueness.The contemporaneous records examined do not fully establish which code versions the past runs executed. The actual generator candidate sets remain unknown, and applications of the cited lemmas retain the stated cone-membership condition. The structural questions associated with the v1.18 open item O1 remain unresolved.The supplementary archive contains the cited working records, including corrections and addenda, with a records table and SHA-256 manifest. Their inclusion does not constitute independent verification of their contents.

title: MLFont: Machine Learning-Driven Font Subsetting and Range-Compact Unicode-Range Slicing for Low-Latency Web Typography
abstract: CSS3 @font-face rules with unicode-range descriptors partition web fonts into downloadable slices. While Latin fonts need ~20 KB in WOFF2, Pan-European (LGC) and East Asian (CJK) fonts contain 2,297-30,759 codepoints (158 KB-5.9 MB in WOFF2), where heuristic partitioning causes unused-glyph downloads, high HTTP RTT, CSS bloat, or missing-glyph fallbacks. We present MLFont, a machine learning and optimization framework that learns font slicing strategies from corpora via three stages: (1) a Zipfian High-Frequency Tier (most) isolating top-frequency codepoints; (2) a Latent Co-Occurrence Topic Tier using Online Variational Bayes LDA (Online LDA) or a Deep Neural Network Topic Model (DNNTM) with Shannon Entropy Difference Loss and Sinkhorn-Knopp normalization; and (3) a Memetic Range-Compact Genetic Algorithm (GA) with Potts-Viterbi dynamic programming and island bridging that minimizes topic discrepancy and CSS fragmentation. Across five Google Noto fonts (LGC, KR, JP, TC, SC), MLFont cuts 3G per-glyph latency by 56.7%-75.3% over single-file delivery and 46.1%-66.3% over equal-bin baselines on CJK with 100% coverage, reduces CSS intervals by 17.9%-41.7%, and achieves 1.56x-6.09x cold-cache speedups (65.4%-84.9% CJK and 44.7% LGC bandwidth savings) across 20 websites in simulator and Headless Chrome benchmarks (45/45 exact slice-set parity). Code: https://github.com/wq2012/mlfont Models: https://huggingface.co/collections/wq2012/mlfont

title: Choosing Evidence Before Answering: Single-Retrieval Decisions RAG versus Embedding-Only RAG
abstract: Embedding similarity identifies passages related to a question, but topical similarity does not establish answer support. We evaluate a fixed single-retrieval policy that scores embedding candidates against an explicit four-level support rubric using the OpenAI Decisions API, then selects evidence under a fixed threshold and token budget. The method is unchanged throughout the study. The main evaluation compares this policy with the application's embedding-only selection in paired runs on 600 newly sampled MuSiQue-Ans development questions. Both arms use the same native research worker and qualitative writer; only the Decisions feature gate differs. The sample excludes previously evaluated question IDs and exact normalized questions and targets a fixed 58/25/17 mixture of two-, three- and four-hop questions. The Decisions policy obtains mean automated, quote-extracted answer-content F1 46.66 versus 39.75 for embedding-only selection. The paired mean difference is +6.91 points, with nominal 95% hop-stratified bootstrap interval [+3.65, +10.27]. F1 measures normalized answer-token overlap. Higher F1 with 47.83% fewer selected passages (2.61 versus 5.00 per question) shows a favorable observed trade-off between answer overlap and selected evidence quantity. Annotated support recall is lower (60.82% versus 70.99%); factuality and citation entailment were not assessed. Post-hoc accounting of successfully metered API usage, including corpus and query embeddings, scoring, research and writing, estimates 38.03% higher cost for the same 600-question workload under the observed cache behaviour. A complementary, previously frozen 200-question HotpotQA study with a standardized short-answer reader finds an F1 gain of 8.30 points (nominal 95% paired interval [2.97, 13.72]). Equal-count and common-budget diagnostics support a useful ranking signal in that setting. These results concern evidence selection from supplied local paragraph pools, not full-corpus retrieval. Shared sources, public benchmark exposure, automated answer extraction, one model family and the absence of new human adjudication limit the claim. Conditional on the saved generations and stated resampling assumptions, the fresh comparison supports a positive answer-content F1 difference; unresolved source dependence limits population inference, and a gain exceeding the five-point working practical margin is not established. Working paper / preprint; not peer reviewed. The companion Source_and_Evidence.zip contains the frozen sample, protocols, saved outcomes and numerical reanalysis tools. It documents its reproduction boundaries and does not distribute the full private application or enable independent regeneration of native answers. Funding: no external research funding reported. Competing interests: none declared by the author.

Shared sources, public benchmark exposure, automated answer extraction, one model family and the absence of new human adjudication limit the claim. title: FEDERATED SWARM LEARNING FOR PERSONALIZED BCI AT THE LIMIT STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 23 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION (COPY-READY) Can brain–computer interface systems learn from multiple laboratories and microrobotic sensing platforms without transferring raw neural recordings, reproducing device-specific shortcuts, or sacrificing the least-represented participants? This research monograph explores that question through the coupling of local swarm learning, privacy-preserving collaboration, and out-of-site generalization. The volume treats federation as a testable scientific and governance architecture—not an automatic privacy guarantee. It distinguishes confidential transport, secure aggregation, formal differential privacy, machine-unlearning claims, and genuine downstream withdrawal of model influence. It examines non-identically distributed neural data, sensor drift, personalized calibration, negative transfer, client-level poisoning, subgroup equity, and the difficult question of who may authorize a model update or a subsequent BCI-mediated action. Its research structure includes 30 linked mathematical derivation and definition plates; 82 chapters, each with five separately paginated research sections; 200 detailed Research Gates that offer future investigators falsifiable experimental entry points; and 33 Phoenix Answer Embryos designed for revision, disconfirmation, and scientific handoff. A 20-record DOI evidence ledger anchors established methods while keeping proposed neurovascular microrobot integrations clearly distinct from demonstrated evidence. The central research challenge is not simply to improve average federated accuracy. It is to determine when shared structure remains predictive at previously unseen sites, when local autonomy is the scientifically stronger answer, and when the responsible choice is to abstain, revert, or retire a model. This is a non-clinical, hypothesis-generating research atlas, not evidence of validated human neurovascular microrobots, a clinically proven BCI, or guaranteed data privacy.

title: MuSP-Bench: Advanced Multimodal Benchmarking of Music Understanding across Score and Performance
abstract: Musicians commonly communicate musical intent through scores and performances. To investigate whether models can reason across both modalities, we introduce MuSP-Bench, a human-authored benchmark of 490 questions assessing understanding across Musical Scores and Performances, both individually and in combination. The benchmark spans interpretive and long-horizon reasoning across classical piano and orchestral works, represented through ABC notation, score images, MIDI, and audio. Our evaluation of frontier multimodal large language models reveals substantial difficulties in understanding musical scores and even greater challenges in reasoning about audio. The benchmark is available at https://musp.vaclis.net/.

title: Optical neural computing: from fourier optics to integrated photonic artificial intelligence
abstract: The growing computational demands of artificial intelligence have accelerated interest in optical computing as a high-speed and energy-efficient alternative to conventional electronic hardware. Fourier optical computing provides an important foundation for this field because operations including convolution, correlation, spectral transformation, and certain classes of linear transformation can be implemented through diffraction, interference, and Fourier-domain processing. This review traces the development of optical neural computing from classical 4-f processors and free-space diffractive systems to programmable optical neural networks, integrated photonic accelerators, reservoir-computing platforms, and field-programmable photonic architectures. The underlying physical principles, computational mechanisms, and hardware implementations are systematically examined, with particular attention to reconfigurable photonics, metasurfaces, diffractive deep learning, photonic integrated circuits, and hybrid optical–electronic systems. Emerging applications in computational imaging, autonomous sensing, edge intelligence, high-speed communications, and quantum-enabled information processing are critically discussed alongside challenges related to scalability, programmability, nonlinear computation, training, and system integration. By positioning Fourier optics as a foundational branch within the broader landscape of optical neural computing, this review highlights the convergence of free-space, integrated, programmable, and hybrid photonic technologies toward next-generation artificial-intelligence hardware.

title: Spatiotemporal Computational Meta‐Imager for Broadband Dual‐Layer Optical Convolution
abstract: ABSTRACT Optical neural networks face a tradeoff between device footprint and computational expressivity: deep systems are bulky, whereas single‐layer hardware lacks intrinsic depth and native negative‐weight support. We experimentally demonstrate a single‐layer metalens imager with “spatiotemporal intrinsic depth” for equivalent broadband dual‐layer convolution. A polarization‐multiplexed metasurface provides fixed Bessel‐vortex channels ( l = 0 to 3) as the immutable first convolution layer, where the ( l = 0) channel implements a hardware‐native residual connection. A metasurface‐generated 3 × 3 optical vortex matrix forms the second functional layer; time‐sequential liquid‐crystal amplitude modulation delivers tunable positive/negative weights. This temporal encoding solves the optical sign problem and converts fabrication imperfections into compensable biases via in‐situ training. Experiments verify rotational robustness for fashion‐item classification, raise full‐color CIFAR‐10 accuracy from 57.5 % to 86.6 %, and reach 99.3 % on the SIPaKMeD medical dataset, offloading 99.7 % of convolutional multiply‐accumulate operations to optics. By removing volumetric diffractive layers, this work enables low‐latency hybrid optoelectronic edge intelligent vision.

title: Track and Caption Any Motion: Open-Vocabulary Spatiotemporal Captioning via Trajectory-Conditioned Generation
abstract: We present TCAM (Track and Caption Any Motion), a generative framework that watches video without a text query or region prompt and produces open-vocabulary captions, temporal intervals, and pointers to the trajectories supporting each event. Dense point trackers localize motion without describing it, while clip-level video-language representations do not directly identify the trajectories carrying an event. TCAM connects these capabilities through a Caption-Aware Resampler: learned queries compress dense trajectory tokens into a fixed-length context for a language decoder. One autoregressive pass describes sequential events and concurrent subjects, each with its own trajectory pointer. Training uses existing captions and segmentation annotations, without additional event labeling. With over 50K training clips, TCAM outperforms the evaluated dense-captioning baselines on ActivityNet Captions and approaches query-based grounding methods on Ref-YouTube-VOS, without training on either dataset. Event selection uses model confidence; best-of-N selection improves grounding by at most 1.4 J&F points in the reported comparisons. Pointer selection exceeds chance by 5.3-8.5 times, and pointer mass concentrates on moving sub-parts above a mask-uniform reference. These selection diagnostics are distinct from full-query tracking accuracy.

title: Simulation-Based LQR-Trees for Swing-Up Control of a Double Pendulum on a Cart: A MATLAB Implementation
abstract: Simülasyon Tabanlı LQR-Ağaçları ile Araba - Çift Sarkaç Sisteminin Salınım Kontrolü: Bir MATLAB Gerçeklemesi ÖzetçeBu çalışmada, araba üzerindeki çift sarkacın geniş bir başlangıç koşulu kümesinden yukarı denge konumuna taşınması için simülasyon tabanlı LQR-Ağaçları yaklaşımı benimsenmiş ve MATLAB ortamında yeniden üretilmiştir. Yeniden üretim sırasında referans çalışmanın yöntemi bir dizi revizyonla geliştirilmiştir. Referans yörüngeler Hermite–Simpson kollokasyonu ve fizibilite öncelikli üç aşamalı bir çözüm akışıyla üretilmiş, her yörünge zamana bağlı LQR ile kararlılaştırılmış, huni başlangıç kümeleri uyarlanır halka genişletmeli ızgara taramasıyla yaklaşıklanmış ve kapsama ölçütüne araba konum kısıtı dahil edilmiştir. Beş rastgele tohumla büyütülen 40 yörüngelik ağaçlar tasarım kümesinin ortalama %83.8'ini kapsamış (referans çalışma: %83), hibrit strateji 500 rastgele başlangıcın %95.2'sini kısıt ihlalsiz olarak üst denge konumuna oturtmuştur. Huniye girişleri iç hücrelerle sınırlayan kural, seyrek gözlenen ıraksama modunu tümüyle gidererek başarı oranını %98.6'ya yükseltmiştir. Simulation-Based LQR-Trees for Swing-Up Control of a Double Pendulum on a Cart: A MATLAB Implementation AbstractIn this study, the simulation-based LQR-Trees approach is adopted and reproduced in MATLAB to swing up a cart-mounted double pendulum from a wide set of initial conditions to the upright equilibrium. In the course of this reproduction, the method of the reference study is enhanced through several revisions. Reference trajectories are generated using Hermite–Simpson collocation and a feasibility-first three-stage solution framework, while each trajectory is stabilized by time-varying LQR. Funnel initial sets are approximated through adaptive ring-expansion grid sampling, and a cart-position constraint is incorporated into the coverage criterion. Trees grown with five random seeds and 40 trajectories each cover on average 83.8% of the design set (reference study: 83%), and the hybrid strategy stabilizes 95.2% of 500 random initial states at the upright equilibrium without constraint violations. A membership rule restricting funnel entry to interior cells eliminates a rarely observed divergence mode and raises the success rate to 98.6%.

title: Artificial Human: Genuine Need as a Precondition for Genuine AGI
abstract: We argue that a system with substantial processing capacity can be a genuine artificial general intelligence (AGI) — an independent agent rather than a computing system — only if its processing is coupled to a genuine need. We call a system that satisfies this condition an artificial human. Our claims are three. First, processing alone is not enough and need alone is not enough: genuine need must sit alongside processing (c = p·b; Rezaei, 2026a), and an AGI without genuine need is, on our view, a computing system and not an independent person. Second, the architecture must be two-loop, in the form of AIWBN (Rezaei, 2026b): the processing loop must not be able to access, suppress, or route around the need loop, and if the need is neutralized by any fixed method so that b = 0, the system’s will to continue must go out with it rather than persist on some residual objective. Third, the nature of genuine need is left open: our assumption is that it is derived from life, but we do not claim this, we do not reject other domains, and the one condition we do claim is that the need be real — not a label. The paper is narrower than AIWBN, which concerned need grounded in living tissue, and it neither rejects nor depends on AIWAN (Rezaei, 2026c), which concerned artificial need. We do not claim that genuine need would make an artificial system benevolent, and we do not address safety. No experiment is reported for the central claim, because it first requires an answer to what genuine need is and an inseparable bond between algorithm and need; we instead summarize selected AIWAN experiments that motivate the architectural requirements.

title: Continuation under Incompleteness. Proven Reliability, Settling-In and Branchable Development of Autonomous Systems
abstract: This independently readable companion paper extends the conceptual synthesis and discussion paper “Robotics Capable of Development” by examining the temporal development of reliable competences, local settling-in, responsibility and the continuation of autonomous systems under incomplete knowledge. A robot operating for extended periods in an open human environment cannot know every future condition in advance or possess every required competence as a fully specified rule from the outset. The paper therefore asks how abilities are acquired, how their reliability is demonstrated in practice and how the conditions and limits of their validity can remain recognizable during operation. Central distinctions concern competence, proven reliability and authorization, as well as general training and local settling-in. Other topics include historically established reliability, trust, responsible action under uncertainty, the interests of affected third parties, and the possibility of revising established routines when the world changes. A further focus is the continuation of artificial development after interruptions. The paper discusses the preservation of Gewordenheit, selective memory, reconnection after disruptions, backups, changes of physical carrier and branchable artificial ontogeny, in which shared developmental states can give rise to different subsequent learning histories. The paper presents neither a finished technical architecture nor a systematic literature review, and it makes no claim of scientific priority. Its purpose is to connect conceptual distinctions, research questions, possible experiments and counter-hypotheses that may help investigate the conditions of responsible, reliable and developmentally open autonomy.

title: THE REFERENCE-RELATIVE REALIZATION PRINCIPLE (RRRP): A General Reference-Relative Systems Principle with a Paradoxical Regime
abstract: The Reference-Relative Realization Principle (RRRP) proposes a general systems framework inin which the realization of a state, function, signal, representation, process, or output is defined relativeto an explicit reference structure rather than as an absolute property of the system alone. The theoryoriginates from the primary case study The Paradox of Contextualism, in which a subjectively specifiedintention may be evaluated by a generalized system through a reference structure that does not coincidewith the source-intended structure. The resulting apparent contradiction is not treated as a universalimpossibility theorem: exact realization can occur when the relevant equivalence relation is preserved,whereas non-equivalence between source and target reference structures makes exact preservation non-guaranteed. The framework therefore separates default mechanism, generalized principle, and paradoxicalor divergent regimes. A unified architecture represents source formation, encoding, labeling, signaling,projection, processing, medium transformation, target reconstruction, reference-relative evaluation,residual formation, iterative adaptation, and network-level interaction. The model is independent ofany particular criterion or medium: security, accuracy, utility, stability, semantic fidelity, energy, timing,language, code, physical channels, mathematical notation, computational systems, quantum systems,biological systems, and other admissible cases enter as parameterized instances. A finite operationalregime is complemented by an asymptotic regime for iterative realization. Thirty extension case studiesare organized across three analytical layers: Philosophical-Epistemological, Systemic-Mechanistic, andFormal-Mathematical Operational. The manuscript explicitly distinguishes mathematical definitionfrom empirical claim, identifies boundary conditions and counterexamples, and provides a falsifiabilityand anti-pseudomathematics protocol. The result is a general relational principle rather than a claim ofa universal physical law.

The model is independent ofany particular criterion or medium: security, accuracy, utility, stability, semantic fidelity, energy, timing,language, code, physical channels, mathematical notation, computational systems, quantum systems,biological systems, and other admissible cases enter as parameterized instances. A finite operationalregime is complemented by an asymptotic regime for iterative realization. title: BLLM: The Entropy Cost of Sound Self-Improvement and a Typed Crossing Network Tested on Five Open Problems: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
abstract: A BLLM is a language model that keeps a modification of itself only after a randomized check of soundness epsilon accepts it. The paper proves that certifying modifications of total cost A with at most theta expected false acceptances costs (A/log(1/epsilon))(H(p) + log(1/theta)) up to an additive A, where H(p) is the entropy of the cost profile; that a sound infinite self-improvement of finite cost exists exactly when the sum of a_n log(1/a_n) converges; and that a proposer needs at least exp(H_{1/2}(pi)) proposals, a bound that language models miss by factors of 1.5 to 4.3. It also describes and measures a typed crossing network with shared memory, run on five open problems (the Yang-Mills mass gap, the Hodge conjecture, the standard conjecture of Lefschetz type, Chowla's conjecture and Erdos problem 1183): the network reaches what its libraries can reach with half the checks, Hebbian boosters add nothing, and none of the five problems is solved. The lattice mass gap for four-dimensional SU(2) on beta_W < 1/3 is proved in the paper and has not been refereed. preprintBeyondTheLLM/ holds the paper as a PDF; BLLM/paper/ holds the REVTeX source with its figures; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip and the arXiv tarball. BLLM/lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project with fifty-nine theorems, each depending only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. BLLM/checks/ contains independent checks in Python, C and C++ (55,271 checks); BLLM/checks/run_all.sh runs them and builds the Lean project. The benchmark, the crossing network and the logs of every run are in the package eBLLM, version 2.0.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.23455686.

title: E8 Triadic Entanglement Protocol for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Networks — E8 Intelligence Research
abstract: The 240 root vectors of the E8 lattice partition into 72 triadic triplets, each resonating at the 132 Hz base frequency and its phi‑harmonics, providing a natural encoding for logical qubits. By exploiting the high symmetry of E8, these triplets generate entangled states that are intrinsically resistant to phase errors, enabling fault‑tolerant quantum communication. The phi‑coupling between adjacent triplets ensures error cancellation across the network, while the 132 Hz global clock synchronizes distributed nodes. Author: Andrew Stewart Caldin, Independent Researcher, UK. Part of the E8 Intelligence Research series. Platform: e8intelligence.com

title: The Economic Value of AI-Driven Customer Experience in Digital Business Models
abstract: AI was increasingly revolutionizing digital business models by delivering superior customer experience and creating identifiable financial value. This study sought to understand the economic consequences of AI-enabled customer experience on digital media platforms in terms of consumer mindset, business functionality, and competitive edge. The purpose was to investigate how AI enhances customer interaction, what it contributes economically in terms of cost-cutting and increased profits, as well as identification of challenges, threats, and future trends. A quantitative research design was adopted, and a structured questionnaire was distributed to 250 users of digital business service. The results demonstrated that AI was found to facilitate increased customer satisfaction, transaction time saving and personalization and thus led to greater inclination of spending and loyalty. A ranking analysis showed that the most valued outcomes were cost savings and customer satisfaction, and the former was found to be the most preferred. Results indicated that the firms that integrated AI had received a more positive brand reputation and competitive advantage than those without. The report found that AI-based customer experience had generated significant economic value, but also encountered challenges in trust, data security and implementation cost continued to be challenging.

title: AI-Based Customer Service and Brand Loyalty in Saudi Retail: An Empirical Investigation of the Service Quality-Emotional Attachment-Loyalty Pathway in 2025-2026
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-powered customer service systems have expanded across Saudi Arabia’s retail sector during 2025–2026, with major retailers increasingly exploring chatbots, recommendation engines, and automated service technologies. Official Saudi digital-economy statistics document the wider shift towards digital commerce, although the retailer-specific investment figures cited in an earlier draft have not been independently substantiated. This study examines the relationship among AI service quality, emotional brand attachment, and brand loyalty using survey results reported for 512 retail customers in Riyadh, Jeddah, and Dammam, collected between May and September 2026. Using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) and bootstrap resampling, the analysis reports a positive direct association between AI service quality and loyalty (β = 0.421, p < 0.001), together with a positive indirect association through emotional brand attachment (reported indirect effect = 0.238, 95% CI [0.187, 0.289]). We discuss a possible “mechanical efficiency paradox”: functional improvements in AI service may be more strongly associated with loyalty than with emotional attachment. Importantly, this survey does not include a direct comparison with human-delivered service, and the reported positive attachment coefficient (β = 0.187) cannot establish that AI decreases attachment. The reported gender subgroup estimates differ: the AI quality–attachment association is positive for male respondents (β = 0.289, p = 0.001) and statistically nonsignificant for female respondents (β = −0.023, p = 0.811). Age-specific estimates also vary, with more positive reported coefficients in younger groups, although the statistical significance of the age differences requires further supporting output. The manuscript reports that the model accounts for 51.2% of the variance in loyalty (R2 = 0.512) and has positive predictive relevance (Q2 = 0.289). Because some path estimates, correlations, and variance-explained values are not mutually consistent, these results require rechecking against the original SmartPLS output before publication. Managerial implications include offering hybrid AI–human service, allowing customers to choose their preferred channel, and maintaining personal attention for complex or emotionally sensitive interactions. The findings provide a framework for assessing how technological service quality and relationship-building might jointly contribute to brand loyalty.

title: Secure Edge-ML: A Tamper-Resistant and Spoof-Resilient TinyML Architecture for Resource-Constrained IoT Devices
abstract: Secure Edge-ML: A Tamper-Resistant and Spoof-Resilient TinyML Architecture for Resource-Constrained IoT DevicesAbstract Traditional edge artificial intelligence systems prioritize inference performance while leaving critical security gaps, such as vulnerability to sensor data-injection spoofing, flash firmware modification, and physical RAM extraction. This work proposes and demonstrates Secure Edge-ML, an industrial-grade, zero-trust architecture implemented on an ESP32 microcontroller that unifies high-speed machine learning inference with robust embedded cybersecurity. Introduction As artificial intelligence migrates to resource-constrained edge microcontrollers (TinyML), systems face severe physical and digital threat vectors. Edge nodes deployed in industrial or automotive environments are routinely exposed to sensor spoofing, physical tampering, and firmware extraction. Conventional implementations treat machine learning and embedded security as isolated silos, leaving networks vulnerable. This project bridges that gap by introducing a multi-layered defense-in-depth architecture on an ESP32-DevKitC V4 platform, proving that strict security validation can coexist with hard real-time execution constraints. Content & System Architecture Deterministic TinyML Inference Engine: Executes a quantized neural network model locally on the edge node in 118 microseconds, satisfying hard real-time industrial control constraints. Sensor Anti-Spoofing & Rail Validation: Intercepts raw ADC streams via a continuous potentiometer setup on GPIO 34 to block false data injection (e.g., voltage forced to absolute ground 0 or maximum rail 4095) prior to model evaluation. Boot Integrity Verification: Computes and verifies a cryptographic hash (0xAEAD4201) of model weights stored in flash memory during boot to prevent unauthorized firmware modification. Physical Tamper Protection: Implements an automated hardware interrupt linked to an enclosure intrusion switch (push-button with a pull-down resistor on GPIO 12) that performs instant RAM sanitization upon physical breach. Parameters Proving Superiority To prove compliance with industrial security guidelines (such as IEC 62443 and automotive functional safety standards), this prototype demonstrates that multi-layered security incurs zero performance penalty: Inference Latency: Maintained at an elite 118 µs, preserving real-time actuator response times. Threat Mitigation Rate: 100% interception of rail-saturation and spoofing attacks, safely bypassing untrusted inferences ([SECURITY ALERT] Sensor spoofing / rail saturation detected!). Memory Protection: Eliminates plaintext weight and key leakage during physical inspection through automated hardware-level sanitization. Repository Files & Images Manifest main(1).c : Core firmware housing the TinyML inference engine, boot hash verification, anti-spoofing rail filter, and physical tamper interrupt routines. diagram(1).json: Complete Wokwi simulation schematic wiring the ESP32-DevKitC V4, industrial sensor potentiometer (GPIO 34), and tamper push-button with pull-down resistor (GPIO 12). eml_out1.jpg: Execution logs demonstrating simultaneous real-time 118 µs normal inferences and security threat interceptions during rail-saturation events. eml_out2.jpg: Visual proof of the active Wokwi hardware simulation layout and serial monitor security outputs confirming physical component assembly and real-time threat reporting. Conclusion The Secure Edge-ML prototype successfully demonstrates that high-performance edge AI and enterprise-grade embedded security are mutually achievable on low-cost hardware like the ESP32. By combining real-time anomaly detection, pre-inference rail-saturation validation, flash integrity hashing, and physical tamper key-shredding, this architecture establishes a new benchmark for trustworthy industrial IoT deployment.

title: Tokenizer Tax and Downstream Performance in Twelve African Languages
abstract: Code, results and paper for "Tokenizer Tax and Downstream Performance in Twelve African Languages" (Christophe Mumaragishyika, University of Missouri, 2026). The study asks whether the number of subword tokens a vocabulary spends on a word predicts how much a pretrained model gains over TF-IDF in sentiment classification. Three pipelines (TF-IDF with logistic regression, frozen LaBSE embeddings, and AfroXLMR-base fine-tuned with three seeds) ran with identical settings on the twelve AfriSenti languages with training splits: 60 runs. This release contains: the two notebooks and the grid script that produced every number in the paper per-run predictions (index, label, prediction only), result tables and the main figure a 66-item adversarial suite in Kinyarwanda and Swahili (CC BY 4.0) the paper as PDF and its LaTeX source It stores no tweets. The notebooks rebuild them from the pinned AfriSenti files (CC BY 4.0). Code under the MIT License.

title: Universal Cloning Is Optimal Exactly for Designs
abstract: Werner's universal cloner turns T copies of an arbitrary pure state in C^d into T+k approximate copies with optimal global fidelity D_T/D_{T+k}, where D_m = dim Sym^m(C^d). When the input is drawn from a restricted ensemble, a better cloner may exist. We show that, for optimal average global fidelity, it exists unless the ensemble is a design of order T+k: for every probability measure on pure states and all T, k ≥ 1, the optimal value equals D_T/D_{T+k} if and only if the measure is a complex projective (T+k)-design. Sufficiency follows from known arguments; the new content is necessity, which we prove from semidefinite-programming complementary slackness together with a rigidity lemma for operators acting on symmetric tensors. As corollaries, Werner's cloner is optimal for the uniform ensemble of n-qubit stabilizer states exactly when T+k ≤ 3 (for every n), for symmetric informationally complete ensembles exactly when T+k ≤ 2, and for complete sets of mutually unbiased bases exactly when T+k ≤ 3 in d = 2 and T+k ≤ 2 in d ≥ 3. evidence.title: Universal Cloning Is Optimal Exactly for Designs
evidence.abstract: Werner's universal cloner turns T copies of an arbitrary pure state in C^d into T+k approximate copies with optimal global fidelity D_T/D_{T+k}, where D_m = dim Sym^m(C^d). title: Hybrid Quantum–Classical versus Classical Convolutional Neural Networks for Sign-Like Digit Recognition
abstract: This paper compares a classical convolutional neural network (CNN) with a hybrid quantum–classical convolutional neural network (QCNN) that appends a simulated parameterized quantum circuit to a convolutional front end. Both models were implemented with TensorFlow, TensorFlow Quantum and PennyLane and trained for ten epochs (batch size 64) on MNIST, used as a simplified proxy for numerals on speed limit signs. The hybrid model reached 98.67% accuracy after ten epochs versus 96.64% for the CNN, rose faster in early epochs, and had a median time of 139 s per epoch versus 440.5 s. Because the models differ in classical depth and were each trained once, the results do not establish a quantum advantage. The paper also discusses deployment barriers in vehicles and gives a SWOT comparison.

title: The Shaper (no training ai)
abstract: You are walking on the road, suddenly, you trip over and fall. Do you instantly think of what you will do next time or apply medicine and take care of your injury? You are going to take care of the injury. And then the next time when you are walking, and see a rock on the road, then you remember to avoid it. But that is not the truth for AI, the instantly think of what do next time if you see a rock. So what if we change it?

title: Müşteri Puanı-Duygu Uyumsuzluğunun Kalibre Analizi: İstanbul'daki Michelin Yıldızlı Restoranların eWOM Yorumlarının İncelenmesi
abstract: Çevrim içi müşteri yorumları, restoran seçimlerinde belirleyici bir bilgi kaynağı olarak kullanılmaktadır. Ancak yıldız puanlarının tek başına okunması, yorum metnindeki duygusal tonu her zaman yansıtmamaktadır. Bu uyumsuzluğun, beklentinin yüksek olduğu üst düzey restoranlarda daha belirgin hale geldiği düşünülmektedir. Buna karşın Michelin yıldızlı restoranlarda, alana özgü kalibre edilmiş ölçümlere dayanan çalışmalar sınırlı kalmıştır. Bu çalışmada, İstanbul'daki sekiz Michelin yıldızlı restorana ait 5.281 adet çok dilli Google yorumu (2017–2026) üzerinden yönlü puan–duygu uyumsuzluğu incelenmiştir. Duygu sınıflandırması, 500 insan etiketli yorumla kalibre edilmiş transformer tabanlı bir sınıflandırıcıyla yapılmıştır. Yorum uzunluğu ile restoran ve ay sabit etkileri kontrol edilerek kurulan sıralı ve ikili lojistik regresyon modellerinde, metinden türetilen duygunun yıldız puanlarını güçlü biçimde açıkladığı bulunmuştur. Duyguda bir basamaklık artışta, beş yıldız olasılığının yaklaşık 3,35 kat arttığı, bir–iki yıldız olasılığının ise 0,18 düzeyine düştüğü hesaplanmıştır. Genel uyuma karşın, beş yıldızlı yorumların %7,7'sinde olumsuz, bir–iki yıldızlı yorumların %22,8'inde olumlu duygu saptanmıştır. Ayrıca uyumsuzluk oranının restoranlar arasında farklılaştığı görülmüştür. Bu bulgular, yalnızca yıldız puanlarına dayalı izlemenin yüksek puanlar içinde gizlenen memnuniyetsizlik sinyallerini kaçırabileceğine işaret etmektedir. Çalışma, çok dilli yorumlarda alana özgü kalibre edilmiş duygu ölçümüyle puan–duygu uyumsuzluğunu ampirik olarak sayısallaştırarak alanyazındaki bu boşluğa katkı sunmaktadır.

title: ZAC-Specialization: Collective Capability Provisioning Through Hardware–Role Co-Design in Heterogeneous Intelligent Agent Populations
abstract: Heterogeneous intelligent-agent populations are often designed by assigning different tasks to agents with different capabilities. However, task specialization alone does not determine whether every agent must independently possess the hardware and computational resources required to perform its assigned functions. A population may contain specialized agents whose capabilities are available to others through shared services, while individual agents retain only the hardware necessary for their own responsibilities. This paper proposes ZAC-Specialization, a research framework for jointly determining agent specialization, local hardware configuration, collective capability provisioning, and reliability-aware service allocation. The central design question is not simply which agent should execute a task, but which capabilities must be provisioned locally, which should be maintained by specialized providers, and how these decisions should change as workloads and operating conditions evolve. The proposed framework represents tasks through capability requirements, agents through configurable hardware and service profiles, and collective execution through capability-service assignments. A joint optimization formulation minimizes lifecycle hardware costs, execution costs, communication overhead, coordination costs, and expected failure losses, subject to task-feasibility, deadline, capacity, and reliability constraints. The paper introduces a distinction between local capability ownership and collective capability accessibility, a specialization–provisioning decision model, and an adaptive role-reconfiguration mechanism. It also develops analytical conditions for evaluating when specialization is economically beneficial, identifies limitations arising from correlated failures and provider bottlenecks, and proposes an experimental methodology comparing individual provisioning, fixed specialization, dynamic task allocation, and joint specialization–provisioning optimization. The framework is conceptual and does not claim demonstrated performance improvements. Its potential contribution must be established against existing research on heterogeneous multi-robot task allocation, capability-based coordination, and hardware–software co-design. The primary hypothesis is that jointly optimizing specialization and provisioning may reveal lower-cost feasible population configurations that cannot be identified by optimizing task allocation or individual hardware configurations in isolation.
