title: Non-Euclidean Toroidal Topography in Large Language Models: Compact Riemannian Manifold Embeddings, Geodesic Attention, and 3D Photonic Co-Simulation Verification
abstract: Conventional Transformer neural networks embed token representations within flat Euclidean latent spaces RD . Despite their empirical utility, Euclidean geometries ex- hibit severe isotropic distance concentration in high dimen- sions, lack periodic boundary-free inductive bias, and scale self-attention quadratically O(N2) over sequence length N. Furthermore, classical inner-product softmax atten- tion inherently suffers from cluster dominance, wherein dif- fuse groupings of irrelevant tokens overpower singular ex- act factual keys, inducing catastrophic hallucination. In this work, we introduce Toroidal Topography Lan- guage Models (TT-LLMs), an architectural paradigm that projects high-dimensional token representations onto a compact 2-Torus Riemannian manifold T2 ∼ = S1 ×S1 embedded within R3, paired with localized tangent vector fields T(θ,ϕ)T2 and 4D quaternionic hyperspherical S3 Hopf fibrations. We prove and demonstrate: (i) Elimination of dynamic coordinate clamping via continuous cyclic periodic coordinates (θ,ϕ) ∈[0,2π)2 evaluated under reg- ularized origin manifolds; (ii) Fractal Golden Ratio (Φ) Rotary Position Embeddings (F-RoPE) that asymp- totically suppress rational harmonic aliasing across arbi- trarily extended sequence horizons (N ≫105) as guaran- teed by Kolmogorov-Arnold-Moser (KAM) dynamical sta- bility theory; (iii) Deterministic Geodesic Resonance Handshakes via high-quality-factor (Q) Lorentzian ker- nels suppressing diffuse cluster interference by >105×; and (iv) Direct physical mapping to integrated silicon photonics via Gaspard Monge’s collinear circle theorem with inward-normal centering and an impedance-matched triple-ring cascade (100 mm →14.14 mm →2 mm). Full 3D Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) Maxwell vec- tor curl simulations verify an empirical loaded resonance factor Qloaded = 2,791.5 at 120 nm coupling gap and an op- tical passive switching energy of 0.0460 fJ/MAC, demon- strating a 21,758.1×core optical energy reduction over electronic GPU multiply-accumulate baselines.

title: Cadre variationnel et géométrique EHK-SCCI pour la sécurisation topologique des réseaux profonds : Un cadre variationnel Einstein–Hilbert–Kayad couplant la courbure d'Ollivier–Ricci, l'expansion spectrale de Ramanujan et la stabilisation de Lyapunov pour l'abstention hors-distribution et adversariale
abstract: Nous présentons EHK-SCCI (Einstein–Hilbert–Kayad / Spectral Graph Geometric Core Realization), un cadre variationnel de sécurisation et d’abstention sélective pour les réseaux neuronaux profonds utilisés dans des contextes critiques. Le cadre modélise la propagation des activations latentes comme un écoulement dissipatif sur une variété riemannienne d’états cachés, munie d’un bord représentant le domaine de fonctionnement nominal. L’action EHK associe un terme de type Einstein–Hilbert, le terme de bord de Gibbons–Hawking–York et une densité de bord contrôlée dépendant d’un invariant spectral-topologique. La variation métrique de cette densité définit un tenseur de contrainte de bord effectif, qui engendre une force de rappel topologique et active un disjoncteur d’abstention. La stabilité de l’erreur latente est établie par une fonctionnelle de Lyapunov associée à la dynamique gradient. La contribution centrale n’est pas l’introduction isolée de la courbure d’Ollivier–Ricci, des graphes de Ramanujan ou de l’analyse de Lyapunov. Elle réside dans leur unification variationnelle : une anomalie géométrique détectée dans le graphe latent déclenche une contrainte dynamique active, une politique d’abstention et une dissipation certifiée de l’erreur.

title: Volume X: The Epistemological Arc: From Dual Clocks to Residual Risk, Molecular Entanglement and Sovereign Pathways
abstract: This tenth volume narrates the epistemological and theoretical arc of the inquiry that began with a dual-clock distinction between an uncertain quantum-advantage timeline and an already-running cryptographic-migration and architectural-integration timeline. Successive volumes established quantum memory specifications, examined modular cryogenic interconnects and cryo-CMOS control as complementary solutions to scaling bottlenecks, quantified molecular entanglement entropy and the purifying effect of fermionic superselection rules, converted residual gaps into readiness indicators, and mapped those indicators onto sovereign pathways, concrete molecular systems and published 2027–2029 roadmaps. The arc demonstrates that usable quantum capability for molecular simulation and cryptographic relevance is governed by a vector of measurable thresholds—logical error, modular memory integration, cryo-CMOS power and superselection overhead—rather than by any single predicted year. The findings supply a practical, dual-clock framework for readiness that remains independent of vendor milestones.

title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
abstract: While LLM agents are increasingly capable of gathering and synthesizing evidence from a single homogeneous source, such as structured tables or unstructured data, real-world analytical questions frequently span heterogeneous sources. For example, answering one enterprise question may require both a result computed over an internal database and evidence found on the web. Recent evaluations on benchmarks like HybridDeepResearch show that even frontier agents struggle when evidence must cross this boundary. While these benchmarks have exposed the limitation, methodologies to explicitly teach cross-source reasoning remain absent. To address this, we introduce HybridResearcher, a 4B agent trained to bridge evidence across the structured and unstructured boundary. To build it, we synthesize cross-source bridge trajectories by starting with validated single-source tasks-such as existing text-to-SQL or web search queries-and fabricating the missing source around a bridge entity drawn from the seed's own output. We retain a sample only when strict construction gates confirm that neither side alone suffices, ensuring the data requires true cross-source interdependence. Finally, we train on this curated dataset using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. Evaluated on the existing HybridDeepResearch benchmark, HybridResearcher improves over our base model, Qwen3.5-4B, by 30.0 points pass@8 and surpasses the far larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B by 8.3 points, while also improving over its base model on established, held-out single-source benchmarks (BrowseComp and BrowseComp-Plus), demonstrating that this complex cross-source reasoning can be taught directly to small models without triggering catastrophic forgetting.

title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
abstract: High-quality image editing requires precise modification of target regions while preserving the content of unrelated regions. Existing editing models produce flattened outputs that limit precise local manipulation and layer reuse, while decomposition methods typically optimize layer recovery separately from instruction-driven editing. To this end, we introduce LayerEditor, a unified framework that couples instruction-guided image editing with controllable generation of reusable RGBA layers. At its core, In-Context RGB-Alpha Token Modeling jointly represents the edited canvas and an ordered sequence of RGB-Alpha layers within a single token sequence, enabling semantic edits and explicit control over individual layer content. To retain the pretrained model's editing capability during adaptation to layered outputs, we propose Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation, which transfers its editing prior to both the edited canvas and the image composed from the predicted layers. To support training and evaluation, we construct LayerEditor-100K, a large-scale paired image-editing dataset with ordered RGBA layer annotations, and introduce dedicated benchmarks for layered editing. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LayerEditor maintains strong editing fidelity while generating accurate RGBA layers, supporting both flexible layer-level manipulation and multi-layer decomposition.

title: Hate Speech dataset
abstract: The Indo-HateSpeech Dataset is a collection of social media comments intended to support research in hate speech detection, abusive language identification, and Natural Language Processing (NLP). The dataset contains 77,926 records of user-generated comments, primarily collected from Instagram-related sources, along with associated metadata such as dates, likes, post identifiers, source information, and classification labels.The dataset includes three label categories: HS0, HS1, and HSN, representing the dataset's original classification scheme. These labels can be used to investigate patterns in online discourse and develop or evaluate machine learning models for identifying potentially hateful or harmful content. The comments include informal language, transliterated Indian languages, and multilingual social media expressions, making the dataset potentially useful for studying language variation and the challenges of automated content moderation. The ContextGuard K2 Ready Dataset is a structured dataset designed for research into context-aware social media analysis, conversational language understanding, and automated content moderation. It contains 2,480 records represented by two columns: Input_Sequence and Target_Score. The Input_Sequence field uses a structured format containing [CONTEXT] and [TARGET] markers. It represents conversational context followed by a target comment or user-generated text. This structure enables research into how preceding messages may influence the interpretation and classification of subsequent content, particularly in discussions involving offensive language, abusive expressions, and potentially harmful online interactions.The Target_Score field contains numerical values of 0.0, 0.5, and 1.0. These scores provide a numerical target for supervised machine learning experiments. Their precise semantic interpretation should be established from the dataset's labeling methodology before assigning specific meanings to individual score values. The ContextGuard SFT Dataset V4 is a supervised fine-tuning (SFT) dataset developed for research and experimentation in automated content moderation, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and multilingual text classification. The dataset contains 760 structured training examples designed to train AI moderation systems to classify user-generated text into three categories: BENIGN, WARN, and ESCALATE.Each record follows a conversational message format consisting of a system instruction, a user-provided text sample, and an assistant response. The system instruction defines the moderation task and specifies the expected output structure. The assistant response contains a reasoning section enclosed intags, followed by a classification decision enclosed intags.The dataset includes Hinglish text and English-language social media comments, including informal expressions, offensive language, potentially harmful statements, and discussions requiring contextual interpretation. This makes it useful for investigating the challenges of moderation across informal, multilingual, and code-mixed language.

title: Holographic Neural Memory Architectures and Distributed Associative Networks: Phase-Encoded Interference, High-Dimensional Vector Representations, and Fault-Tolerant Recall
authors: Akash-B. Atapi, Man Mohit, Dr. Vishal Shrivastava, Dr. Vibhakar Pathak, Er. Amit Kumar Tiwari
abstract: Modern neural network architectures—ranging from deep transformers to recurrent networks—rely predominantly on localized, addressable weight matrices stored in physical RAM or high-bandwidth memory (HBM). While effective for general inference, localized memory architectures exhibit catastrophic fragility under random memory corruption, lack graceful degradation when subjected to hardware bit-flips, and scale inefficiently when forming distributed associative bindings across millions of abstract concepts. Holographic Neural Memory (HNM) and HighDimensional Vector Symbolic Architectures (VSA / Hyperdimensional Computing) establish a transformative non-local computing paradigm inspired by optical holography and distributed brain memory. By encoding symbolic information into high-dimensional hypervectors (d >= 10,000) via random orthogonal projections and superimposing associations through complex phase-encoded interference, HNM architectures distribute information uniformly across every spatial component of the memory vector. This superposition property grants remarkable fault tolerance: distributed associative memories can experience up to 45% total vector component corruption or hardware bit-erasure while still executing clean pattern completion, un-aliased retrieval, and robust compositional reasoning. However, scaling holographic memories to enterprise foundation models introduces severe computational and mathematical bottlenecks: noise accumulation and crosstalk interference during massive vector superpositions, dimensionality curse during multi-hop role-filler binding, and complex hardware mapping onto conventional von Neumann processors. This paper delivers an exhaustive, mathematically formal technical investigation and empirical benchmark of holographic neural memory architectures. We formalize phase-encoded circular convolution binding, derive signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) capacity bounds under random hypervector superposition, and model fault-tolerant pattern recall. Furthermore, we construct an enterprise software and hardware-in-the-loop testbed evaluating holographic memory layers integrated with transformer residual streams across massive relational retrieval tasks, multi-modal concept grounding, and radiation-hardened edge aerospace workloads. Our empirical findings demonstrate that holographic neural memories achieve 99.2% robust associative recall under 40% random bit corruption, outperforming conventional hash tables and key-value caches by orders of magnitude in resilience, while sustaining sub-microsecond retrieval latencies on dedicated processing-in-memory (PIM) accelerators. Finally, we formulate open challenges in non-linear compositional generalization, continuous-time hypervector dynamics, and alloptical holographic processor hardware realization

title: ZAPP: a zero-aware photovoltaic power prediction framework
abstract: Predicting photovoltaic power generator outputs is not easy, especially when the values are near zero, because even very small errors can lead to large percentage errors. We introduce a new forecasting framework, ZAPP (Zero-Aware Photovoltaic Power Predictor), that handles near-zero errors while maintaining high prediction accuracy. The model does not rely on a single unified regression model but instead attaches two refinement stages to a base regression model. The first stage, called ZeroGate, predicts whether the output should be zero. The second refinement stage, the low-power MAPE reducer, fine-tunes the non-zero outputs near the zero level without significantly affecting scale-dependent regression metrics. The datasets are divided into training, validation, and test sets in chronological order, ensuring that test data is not used during model development, threshold tuning, ensemble weighting, or calibration. Experimental evaluation included base models such as Persistence, Ridge, XGBoost, LSTM, Transformer, and a hybrid Ridge–XGBoost model. Two separate datasets are employed to strengthen the quality of the results. For the hybrid model, sMAPE fell from 60.57% to 11.07% on Dataset 1. Its final MAE, RMSE, and R 2 were 22.37, 60.72, and 0.9637, respectively. On Dataset 2, sMAPE decreased from 63.30% to 11.92%, with MAE = 52.24, RMSE = 144.60, and R 2 = 0.9559. The zero-aware correction mainly reduced percentage errors without weakening the overall regression results.

title: Gaussian Process Bandits with Paired Auxiliary Observations
abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used for expensive black-box optimization, yet observation noise makes each evaluation less informative and slows posterior learning. Standard BO learns from costly outcomes gathered during optimization. In many applications, however, low-cost auxiliary data are available beforehand. We introduce Auxiliary-Informed Gaussian Process Bandit (AI-GPB), a variance-reduction method that combines an offline estimate of the auxiliary mean with a correction coefficient learned from paired online observations. Notably, it exploits correlation between paired observation errors without requiring the auxiliary mean to approximate the objective. We establish finite-sample GP confidence bounds and regret guarantees, including explicit cumulative and simple regret rates for Matérn kernels. Numerical experiments across continuous BO benchmarks with varied landscapes and dimensions show consistent reductions in cumulative and simple regret relative to vanilla GP-UCB, even when within-pair correlation is moderate and the auxiliary mean is estimated from noisy offline data.

title: Boundary: Universal Continuity and Recoverability Sciences — Complete Canonical Framework
abstract: Boundary: Universal Continuity and Recoverability Sciences — Complete Canonical Framework Noelia Sofia Sanchez | Interval Studio | 2026 Overview Boundary presents the consolidated canonical framework of Continuity Science, Recoverability Science, and Recoverability-Constrained Systems, developed across an interconnected body of formal publications, computational structures, technical architectures, scientific disciplines, constitutional instruments, and interdisciplinary applications. This edition integrates the established internal architecture and documented publication lineage into a unified reference distribution. It preserves foundational works, formal definitions, conditional theorems, analytical matrices, implementation frameworks, governance instruments, and subsequent canonical extensions. Boundary addresses a fundamental operational question: under what conditions can a system undergo change, intervention, interruption, transformation, delegation, or succession while retaining admissible, executable paths to protected future states? Scientific Foundations The framework connects: Recoverability Science: admissible continuation under irreversibility constraints. Continuity Science: preservation and transformation of materially significant identity, state, relationships, capabilities, and successor possibilities. Continuity Mathematics: successor-state structures, finite reachability, protected target sets, recovery boundaries, invariants, abstraction, and proof obligations. Continuity Ontology: existence, distinction, identity, relation, state, transition, boundary, and persistence. Distinction and Materiality Science: identification and preservation of operationally consequential differences. Recursive Systems Governance: self-application of admissibility, evidence, accountability, and recoverability conditions to evaluators, controllers, institutions, and successor systems. Canonical Mathematical Structure Let C*(X) represent the admissibly reachable successor structure of a modeled state X, and let G denote a specified protected target class. Relative recoverability is represented by: R(X,G) = 1 if and only if C(X) ∩ G ≠ ∅.* The framework distinguishes conceptual possibility from executable recovery, incorporating temporal constraints, detection, intervention, authority, resources, independence, provenance, verification, and operational feasibility. Before an irreversible boundary, the governing criterion concerns preservation of admissible recoverable futures. Where the original protected state can no longer be recovered, continuation is assessed through the greatest recoverable remainder, including containment, correction, reconstruction, substitution, remedy, compensation, adaptation, and successor obligations. Mathematical results are presented according to their declared assumptions, definitions, derivations, proofs, and limits. Integrated Sciences and Architectures The consolidated framework incorporates formal, computational, technological, biological, cognitive, ecological, economic, institutional, and civilizational continuity. Its disciplinary architecture encompasses epistemic continuity, systems engineering, artificial intelligence continuity, computational recoverability, materials and infrastructure, health systems, agency and consent, identity and sovereignty, finance and livelihoods, environmental resilience, collective governance, intergenerational protection, and continuity of knowledge. Technical architectures address controlled transitions, safe interruption, isolation, execution verification, monitoring, recovery, successor handover, evidence integrity, and recursive supervision. Computational Canon The edition includes multiple canonical and historical analytical releases, including million-intersection matrices, nine-direction evaluations, scenario classifications, dependency mappings, proof audits, evidence registers, computational methods, and recursive closure assessments. Each version retains its documented scope and evaluation rules. Apparent disagreements between releases are preserved for reconciliation instead of being silently converted into equivalence. Constitutional and Institutional Architecture The framework incorporates the Universal Continuity and Recoverability constitutional materials, model governance principles, human-rights protections, obligations concerning agency and consent, institutional accountability, and mechanisms for lawful succession, remedy, compensation, and review. Constitutional, legislative, contractual, technical-standard, and international adoption materials are distinguished according to their applicable legal and institutional status. Living-System and Successor Continuity The living-system architecture integrates individual, collective, organizational, ecological, and intergenerational continuity. Recognition, protection, dignity, identity, agency, informed consent, representation, and remedies are treated as distinct obligations. Recognition may ground duties of protection without independently proving a particular scientific theory of consciousness. The framework further examines continuity across biological, technical, social, and future-developed forms of organization, maintaining evidence distinctions where empirical knowledge remains incomplete. Recursive Closure The canonical integration sequence is: DISTINCTION → MATERIALITY → RECOVERABILITY → SUCCESSOR CONTINUITY → RECURSIVE VERIFICATION → META-CLOSURE → LOCAL SILENCE Local silence signifies analytical closure under declared distinctions, evidence, rules, and scope. It is not a declaration that future science, counterexamples, or discovery are impossible. Any materially new evidence, dependency, counterexample, protected interest, or successor condition reopens the analysis. Consolidated Distribution This Zenodo record provides the Boundary canonical framework in eight independent ZIP archives, accompanied by an inventory and verification manifest. The distribution consolidates its foundational scientific work, formal research structures, technical systems, constitutional architecture, computational material, meta-sciences, and canonical extensions into a single citable record. It serves as a reference edition for the continuing development, examination, implementation, and critical evaluation of the Boundary framework. Status: Consolidated published-framework edition. Formal, empirical, technical, and legal claims retain their respective evidence and validation requirements.

title: A Structured Toponym Lexicon of Bukhara Region: An Annotated Onomastic Resource for Low-Resource Uzbek
abstract: A structured, machine-readable toponym lexicon of Bukhara region, Uzbekistan, andcompanion dataset to the paper of the same name. It holds 3,060 records standingfor 3,360 name occurrences across 16 types of geographic object (settlements,mahallas, cemeteries, hills, canals and others). Each record is annotated withobject type, district, structure, and matched indicator and component elements;the etymological fields of the scheme are reserved for later expert work. Thelexicon is built from the toponym material of Kilichev's DSc dissertation on thetoponyms of Bukhara region (Bukhara State University, 2024) with a singledeterministic pipeline that repairs mixed Cyrillic and Latin script and unifiesapostrophes to the official Uzbek modifier letters (oʻ and gʻ use U+02BB; theglottal tutuq belgisi uses U+02BC). Files: the lexicon CSV, the normalizationrules, a README and a licence. See README for the full column dictionary, scopeand citation.

title: One Language, Two Unequal Scripts: Separating Orthography from Information in Multilingual Representations with Punjabi
abstract: Multilingual models are said to abstract away script in their middle layers. Tests usually compare languages that differ in script and language at once. Punjabi does not. It is written in Gurmukhi and in Shahmukhi, which differ in what they record, since unvocalised Shahmukhi leaves short vowels and gemination unwritten. In a public recreation of XLM-R's training data, Shahmukhi Punjabi is about 1% as frequent as Gurmukhi. We use this pair to separate script form from missing information in four encoders. Every statistic is compared with the same architecture under random weights and bootstrapped over sentences. Four Gurmukhi controls remove information in steps. title: VisR-RAG-Fin: Benchmarking Multimodal RAG over Visually Rich Financial Documents
abstract: Enterprise documents such as financial reports are increasingly processed by automated systems, yet they are primarily designed for human reading and exhibit complex visual structure, combining dense text with tables, charts, diagrams, and rich layouts. These characteristics pose significant challenges for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems, which must retrieve relevant pages and leverage visual and structural information during answer generation. Despite recent advances in multimodal retrieval and vision-language models, there remains a limited understanding of how design choices across retrieval and generation components affect end-to-end RAG performance on visually rich documents. In this paper, we present a comprehensive empirical study of multimodal RAG for page-level Question Answering (QA) over financial documents. We introduce VisR-RAG-Fin (Visually Rich RAG for Finance), an open-source benchmark constructed through a general pipeline for visually rich documents that preserves original layout and visual content. Using this benchmark, we systematically analyze retrieval and generation behavior under text-only, multimodal, and hybrid configurations, providing a foundation for rigorous evaluation of RAG systems on complex enterprise document collections. Overall, this work provides actionable insights for practitioners designing and evaluating multimodal RAG pipelines over complex, visually rich enterprise documents.

title: How Does Muon Work in Private Deep Learning? Scalable Differentially Private Training via Orthogonalization
abstract: Training deep neural networks requires optimizers that balance computational efficiency with formal data privacy. While orthogonalized update rules, such as the recently introduced Muon optimizer, have shown strong empirical performance and scalability, their behavior under Differential Privacy (DP) is not yet understood. In this paper, we propose DP-Muon, a differentially private variant of the Muon optimizer. By analyzing Muon's orthogonalized updates through the lens of a Linear Minimization Oracle (LMO), we show that the leading effect of per-example clipping is a positive rescaling of the gradient, to which the LMO is blind, so that only a small directional residual controlled by the centered gradient variance enters the optimization error. This yields an $\mathcal O(K^{-1/4})$ convergence rate, up to logarithmic factors, to a clipping-dependent neighborhood at a fixed noise scale and, with noise calibrated to a fixed $(\varepsilon,δ)$ budget, the standard $(\sqrt d/(n\varepsilon))^{1/2}$ privacy--utility bound of DP-SGD, without assuming bounded gradients. Furthermore, we investigate the hyperparameter landscape of DP-Muon and document how the optimal learning rate, momentum, and batch size change under privacy. Empirically, on image classification DP-Muon matches or improves on DP-SGD and DP-Adam, whereas on language modeling the best optimizer depends on the batch size, with DP-Muon best at small batches and DP-Adam best near the privacy-optimal batch size.

title: Reinforcement Learning for Preventable Hospitalization and Readmission Reduction: A Structured Narrative Review
abstract: Purpose: To critically assess reinforcement learning (RL) for sequential interventions designed to reduce preventable hospitalizations and readmissions, distinguishing computational feasibility from demonstrated clinical effectiveness. Methods: A structured narrative review synthesized direct utilization-focused policies, adjacent inpatient decision policies, and contextual prediction research through 9 October 2026. Outcomes, Markov decision formulations, off-policy estimators, and methodological limitations were analyzed without meta-analysis. Results: Directly relevant peer-reviewed evidence centers on Medicaid care management and post-discharge intervention planning. A retrospective state-action-reward-state-action (SARSA) study estimated a 12-percentage-point reduction in an emergency visit and hospitalization composite; however, this reflects a model-based counterfactual estimate rather than an observed randomized treatment effect. A larger offline study reported non-inferiority on a shaped reward scale alongside narrower intervention-allocation disparities. Data-pooling research contributed theoretical regret bounds and empirical support for learning across patient classes. Critical limitations across the literature include unmeasured confounding, limited action support, surrogate rewards, overlapping cohorts, and absent external validation. No direct study established a prospective randomized reduction in hospitalizations from an executed RL policy. Conclusion: RL provides a coherent framework for longitudinal care allocation, but current evidence supports algorithmic development rather than proven clinical efficacy. Translation demands explicit endpoint definitions, rigorous off-policy evaluation, prospective silent workflow evaluation, and controlled trials with safety, equity, and resource constraints.

title: Verifier-Bound Rule Discovery: A Pre-Registered Evaluation of LLM Proposers for Combinatorial Scheduling
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as proposers of human-readable rules in scientific discovery and combinatorial optimization (FunSearch, ARCHE, SVBRD-LLM). Yet the LLM-proposer systems we surveyed share a methodological gap: none reports a same-budget random-proposer control, none pre-registers its acceptance criteria, and none evaluates at distribution scale –- ARCHE validates on three hand-picked cases, and SVBRD-LLM, the closest system to ours, is outperformed on accuracy by a black-box LSTM while reporting no significance tests. We apply a verifier-bound rule-discovery framework in which an LLM proposes interpretable rules (linear weight vectors and sandboxed programs), an independent programmatic verifier checks domain-hard properties, holdout evaluation is physically isolated and executed exactly once, and every acceptance criterion is frozen before experiments run.
